question.prompt: How many ordered pairs of positive real numbers \((a,b)\) satisfy the equation \[ \begin{gathered} (1+2a)(2+2b)(2a+b)\\ {}=32ab? \end{gathered} \]

solutions.title: Force equality in AM-GM
solutions.explanation:
Each factor on the left is a sum of two positive terms. Applying AM-GM to those three sums produces exactly the right-hand side.

For positive numbers \(u,v\), AM-GM states that \(u+v\ge2\sqrt{uv}\), with equality exactly when \(u=v\). Therefore
\[
1+2a\ge2\sqrt{2a},\qquad
2+2b\ge4\sqrt b,\qquad
2a+b\ge2\sqrt{2ab}.
\]
Multiplying these positive inequalities gives
\[
(1+2a)(2+2b)(2a+b)
\ge16\sqrt{2a}\sqrt b\sqrt{2ab}
=32ab.
\]
If any of the three inequalities is strict, their product is also strict. Thus the given equation requires equality in all three:
\[
1=2a,\qquad 2=2b,\qquad 2a=b.
\]
The first two give \(a=\tfrac12\) and \(b=1\), which also satisfy the third. Conversely, these values make all three inequalities equalities, so they satisfy the original equation.

There is exactly \(\boxed{1}\) ordered pair, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

solutions.title: Rewrite as a sum of squares
solutions.explanation:
The substitution \(x=2a\), \(y=b\) makes the factors more symmetric and allows us to express the equation as a sum of nonnegative terms. Both \(x\) and \(y\) are positive.

After substituting and dividing by \(2\), the equation becomes
\[
(1+x)(1+y)(x+y)=8xy.
\]
Divide by \(xy>0\) and expand:
\[
2+x+\frac1x+y+\frac1y+\frac xy+\frac yx=8.
\]
Subtracting \(8\) and grouping into perfect squares yields
\[
\frac{(x-1)^2}{x}
+\frac{(y-1)^2}{y}
+\frac{(x-y)^2}{xy}=0.
\]
Every numerator is a square and every denominator is positive. Thus every term is nonnegative, and their sum can be zero only if each term is zero. The first two terms force \(x=y=1\), which also makes the third term zero.

All transformations were reversible, so this gives exactly one solution of the original equation:
\[
(a,b)=\left(\frac12,1\right).
\]
The number of ordered pairs is \(\boxed{1}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
